text.title: Learning Speed as Competitive Moat Core Rules
text.summary: 14 testable rules grounding Learning Speed as Competitive Moat plus the universal skip/run routing pair (referenced by the decision tree). The learning-speed moat model: signal collection, versioned belief tracking, weekly rituals, and the decision-log practice that compounds the advantage over time.

section.title: Background
section.p: Learning Velocity = (Signals Noticed x Update Speed x Execution Quality) / Time. Each factor is addressable: signal collection is automated; update speed is increased by weekly reviews instead of quarterly; execution quality is maintained via the belief-update constraint (mutate only on sufficient evidence).

Weekly rituals. Monday: customer interview insights shared. Wednesday: competitor updates reviewed. Friday: experiment results analyzed and strategy adjustments communicated. Time-box rituals: Monday 30 min digest, Friday 45 min strategy. Drift past those times and people skip.

rule.statement: The org MUST maintain a versioned register of active product beliefs (assumption, confidence, source, last-updated); beliefs older than 90 days without update MUST be flagged.
rule.rationale: Implicit beliefs cannot be updated; without a register the org cannot tell whether it is learning or repeating yesterday's bets.

rule.statement: Every strategic decision MUST cite at least one outside-view input (competitor move, market data, customer signal) alongside any inside-view reasoning.
rule.rationale: Inside-view-only decisions cluster on the loudest voice; outside view is the structural counter to founder narrative gravity.

rule.statement: Every reversible decision MUST be logged in a decision journal with date, alternatives considered, expected outcome, and review date; review-date no-shows are a tracked metric.

rationale.source: Shane Parrish — Farnam Street decision journal

rule.rationale: Without a journal, hindsight bias rewrites past decisions to look smart; the journal is the only feedback loop for calibration.

rule.statement: Every product bet MUST have pre-registered kill criteria (signal threshold + observation window); bets without kill criteria are forbidden.
rule.rationale: Without kill criteria, sunk-cost reasoning keeps bets alive past their evidence window; pre-registration is the only structural gate.

rule.statement: The org MUST hold a weekly 30-minute belief-update ritual where each bet's confidence is re-scored against the week's signals; missed weeks count against the moat.
rule.rationale: Beliefs that update on a yearly planning cycle are slower than competitor cycles; weekly is the minimum cadence to compound a learning moat.

rule.statement: Treat beliefs.yaml as code: versioned in git, PR-reviewed, diffable. PR-reviewed belief changes beat Slack-thread consensus.
rule.rationale: Beliefs that live in Notion pages or Slack threads drift without audit trail. A versioned YAML file makes every belief change visible, attributable, and reversible.

rule.statement: Limit the watchlist: 3–5 competitors, 1 macro trend, 1 customer segment. Broader scope equals noise, not signal.
rule.rationale: AI can ingest thousands of signals per day; without a bounded watchlist the team drowns in volume and stops acting on any of it. Constraint is the design.

rule.statement: Ingest at least one external corpus (product analytics or competitor scrape). A system fed only internal Slack channels measures its own opinion velocity, not the market.
rule.rationale: Confirmation loops where the same channel provides signals and classification are invisible and common. External corpus is the mitigation.

rule.statement: Mutate a belief only if (a) 3 or more independent event_ids agree, or (b) 1 high-severity event directly contradicts the current claim with a cited URL or transcript.
rule.rationale: Single data points are noise; three independent signals from different sources constitute evidence. The threshold prevents recency over-weighting and Sonnet evidence-laundering.

rule.statement: Pair every belief with a kill criterion and a check-back date. Beliefs without falsifiers rot into dogma.
rule.rationale: A belief that cannot be falsified is not a belief — it is an assumption. Kill criteria and check-back dates force the team to revisit rather than defend.

rule.statement: Measure decisions made per week crossed with decisions reversed within 30 days. High reversal rate indicates a noisy loop; low decision count indicates an inert org.
rule.rationale: Insights captured is a vanity metric. Decision count and decision stability are the actual outputs of a functioning learning system.

rule.statement: Run quarterly calibration: grade past predictions against outcomes. Recalibrate confidence weights and prompt scoring rubrics based on accuracy.
rule.rationale: Without calibration, confidence weights become superstition. Calibration is not optional — it is the mechanism that prevents the belief system from drifting from reality.

rule.statement: Default to "kill" on the Friday review for evidence-thin roadmap items. Burden of proof is on keeping, not killing.
rule.rationale: Keeping an item with thin evidence consumes H1 capacity. The asymmetric default (keep requires evidence, kill does not) prevents roadmap accumulation.

rule.statement: Separate mechanical work (haiku: signal collection, classification, decision logging) from judgment work (opus: strategy review, roadmap pass). Mixing costs 10x and introduces bias.
rule.rationale: Opus applied to classification tasks burns budget without improving quality. Haiku applied to strategy synthesis produces confident-sounding but shallow reasoning. Each model tier has a specific function.

rule.statement: If preconditions in `## Applies If` do not ALL hold OR any disqualifier in `## Skip If` fires, the agent MUST skip this methodology and document the skip reason in the cycle artefact.
rule.rationale: A minimum-form decision tree must route 'preconditions-not-satisfied' to skip; this rule is the canonical target.

rule.statement: If preconditions in `## Applies If` ALL hold AND no disqualifier fires, the agent MUST run the methodology end-to-end and produce the artefact specified in 02-output-contract.xml.
rule.rationale: Pair to skip-this-methodology; together they form the always-present minimal route.
